lines: Good afternoon. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
The Manitoba Métis Federation says it’s appalled by the lack of Métis-specific funding in Prime Minister Mark Carney’s new budget, The Canadian Press reports.
A powerful storm system is expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds to B.C.’s coast Friday, with rainfall warnings in parts of Metro Vancouver, CityNews Vancouver reports.
A 14-metre white spruce from Nova Scotia will soon be cut and shipped to Boston as an annual Christmas gift to thank the city for its help after the Halifax Explosion, The Canadian Press reports.

The 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, was arrested Friday morning in Florida on a charge of possessing child sexual abuse material in storage units in California, authorities said.

Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks, The Canadian Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.

bds.h: Tesla pulls the plug on Cybertruck production
bds.lede: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks.
rows: Musk said the decision was taken in order to make room for increased production of its Cybercab robotaxi. The move comes after years of weaker-than-expected sales for the futuristic electric pickup.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the electric car maker will halt production of its Cybertruck next year and prioritize self-driving taxis.
Released in 2023, the truck has become a symbol to some of opposition to Musk amid foray into US politics.
The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.
